title: What's trending on the internet this week? 8 trends (Nov 16–22, 2026)
answer: GTA 6's launch dominated the internet in the week of Nov. 16–22, 2026, from review-bombing to a rumor that Lucia cheats on Jason. People also mourned Fiona the hippo, shrugged off a Nov. 17 blackout scare, copied the "Talk to me Doja" dance, said "huss," tried to move the Bean, wore pajamas to the movies and threw mustard at Lane Kiffin.
body:
How we built this list: from our trend radar's data (new Google search suggestions, Know Your Meme, Bluesky, Mastodon and other sources), with every trend checked against at least two reliable sources.

1. The GTA 6 backlash. Grand Theft Auto VI came out Nov. 19, and critics gave it a 99 on Metacritic, but players complained about 30 fps on consoles and slower missions, and some flooded the user score with low ratings, calling the game "woke." Our radar first saw "why are people saying gta 6 is bad" on Nov. 18 and the "woke" questions on Nov. 20. Explainers: https://trendrundown.com/x/why-are-people-saying-gta-6-is-bad and https://trendrundown.com/x/why-are-people-saying-gta-6-is-woke

2. "Lucia cheats on Jason." A day after launch, players began asking whether GTA 6's Lucia cheats on her partner Jason. Guides that finished the story say she doesn't; the rumor comes from scenes built to plant doubt. First radar signal: Nov. 20. Explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/why-are-people-saying-lucia-cheats-on-jason

3. RIP Fiona. The Cincinnati Zoo announced on Nov. 19 that Fiona the hippo, famous since her premature birth in 2017, had died at age 9 after swallowing a visitor's knit hat. Tributes filled every platform. First radar signal: Nov. 20. Explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/why-are-people-saying-rip-fiona

4. The Nov. 17 blackout scare. Viral posts claimed hackers would shut down banks and the power grid on Tuesday, Nov. 17. Nothing like that happened, though Apple had a real outage that afternoon and other services had glitches the same week. First radar signal: Nov. 16. Explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/why-is-everyone-freaking-out-about-november-17

5. "Talk to me Doja." A TikTok dance in which people copy a bashful sway from the 2015 anime "Yamada-kun and the Seven Witches," set to a sped-up clip of Doja Cat's "Like That." Explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/what-is-the-talk-to-me-doja-trend

6. "Huss." Slang for the quick breaths you make while sprinting, and by extension for running hard or hustling, spread by the "huss huss huss" TikTok trend. Our radar picked up "what does it mean when someone says huss huss huss" on Nov. 22. Explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/what-does-huss-mean

7. Moving the Bean. An anonymous invite asked Chicagoans to push Cloud Gate, the 110-ton "Bean," seven inches to the left; crowds showed up, it didn't budge, and St. Louis tried the same with its Gateway Arch. First radar signal: Nov. 16. Explainer: https://trendrundown.com/x/why-are-people-trying-to-move-the-bean

8. Pajamas and mustard. Fans wore pajamas to early-morning "Sunrise Screenings" of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" on Nov. 21 after the official Hunger Games TikTok suggested it (first radar signal: Nov. 19). The same night, Tennessee fans threw mustard and golf balls during a 27-13 win over Lane Kiffin's LSU, a grudge that dates to 2021 (first radar signal: Nov. 22). Explainers: https://trendrundown.com/x/why-are-people-wearing-pajamas-to-sunrise-on-the-reaping and https://trendrundown.com/x/why-are-people-throwing-mustard-at-lsu
